subject: Archaeology
title: The Bent Pyramid: A Mistake in Stone
description: One-minute skill: The Bent Pyramid: A Mistake in Stone.

hook.text: One pyramid in Egypt changes angle halfway up. It looks like someone made a mistake and kept going.

buildup.text: Pharaoh Sneferu started the Bent Pyramid at Dahshur around 2600 BCE with a steep 54-degree angle.

discovery.text: Cracks appeared as the weight increased. The builders abruptly shifted to a gentler 43-degree angle.

twist.text: Sneferu did not give up. He built a second pyramid nearby — the Red Pyramid — and got it right.

climax.text: The Red Pyramid became the first true smooth-sided pyramid. Sneferu's failure taught Egypt to build perfectly.

punchline.text: Egypt's greatest architectural leap came from learning what went wrong.

quiz.question: Why does the Bent Pyramid change angle halfway up?
options: The pharaoh wanted a unique artistic design
Cracks appeared, forcing builders to reduce the angle to prevent collapse
A new pharaoh took over and changed the plans

details.summary: The Bent Pyramid at Dahshur changes angle midway up, shifting from 54 to 43 degrees. Built for Pharaoh Sneferu around 2600 BCE, the angle change likely reflects engineers correcting structural problems mid-construction rather than repeating an earlier collapse.
details.whyItMatters: The Bent Pyramid captures trial-and-error engineering in stone. It shows that even ancient Egypt's greatest builders learned from mistakes, bridging the gap between the Step Pyramid and the true pyramids at Giza.
takeaways: The pyramid changes angle from 54 to 43 degrees midway up
Built for Sneferu, it reflects mid-construction corrections
It bridges the Step Pyramid and Giza's true pyramids

faq.question: Why did the builders change the pyramid's angle?
faq.answer: The original steep angle likely caused structural instability or cracking. Engineers reduced the angle mid-build to prevent collapse. Some scholars believe the nearby Meidum Pyramid's collapse influenced the decision to play it safe at Dahshur.

faq.question: Did Sneferu build other pyramids after the Bent Pyramid?
faq.answer: Yes. Sneferu built the Red Pyramid nearby at Dahshur, Egypt's first successful true pyramid with smooth sides at a consistent 43-degree angle. He built more pyramids than any other pharaoh, perfecting the form his son Khufu would use at Giza.
